cases.name: case01_reset_omission
cases.spec: The register q shall reset to 0 whenever rst_n is low. When rst_n is high and en is 1, q shall capture din on the next rising clock edge.

golden_sva.expected_behavior: Whenever reset is sampled low, q must already be 0 in that same sampled cycle.

cases.name: case02_grant_delay
cases.spec: grant shall reflect req in the same cycle at each rising clock edge after reset is released.

golden_sva.expected_behavior: After reset is released, each sampled grant must match the previous sampled req with no extra register stage.
golden_sva.temporal_type: cycle-by-cycle invariant with history reference (registered req/grant relation)

cases.name: case03_valid_ready_or_bug
cases.spec: Output transfer is legal only when valid_i and ready_i are both high. valid_o must not assert when only one of them is high.

golden_sva.sva: assert property (@(posedge clk) disable iff (!rst_n) ((valid_i && !ready_i) || (!valid_i && ready_i)) |-> (!valid_o));
golden_sva.expected_behavior: If exactly one of valid_i or ready_i is high, valid_o must stay low; output validity is legal only for a full valid_i && ready_i handshake.

cases.name: case04_fsm_transition
cases.spec: State machine transitions: IDLE->BUSY on start, BUSY->DONE on finish, DONE->IDLE in the next cycle.

golden_sva.expected_behavior: If finish is sampled high, then on the next sampled cycle the FSM must be in DONE rather than having skipped directly back to IDLE.

cases.name: case05_counter_boundary
cases.spec: Counter increments when en is high and wraps to 0 only when cnt equals limit.

golden_sva.sva: assert property (@(posedge clk) disable iff (!rst_n) (en && (cnt != limit)) |=> (cnt == ($past(cnt) + 3'd1)));
golden_sva.expected_behavior: While en is high and cnt has not yet reached limit, the next sampled cnt must equal the previous sampled cnt plus 1.
golden_sva.temporal_type: non-overlapping implication with history reference (increment until limit)

cases.name: case06_priority_encoder
cases.spec: Priority encoder shall grant the highest-index asserted request bit first: req[3] > req[2] > req[1] > req[0].

golden_sva.expected_behavior: Whenever any request bit was high in the previous sampled cycle, the current sampled grant must be the one-hot encoding of the highest-index asserted bit from that previous sampled req vector.
golden_sva.temporal_type: overlapping implication with history reference (general highest-priority one-hot grant rule)

cases.name: case07_fifo_full_boundary
cases.spec: FIFO count increases on write when not full and decreases on read when not empty. full is true only when count equals 4.

golden_sva.expected_behavior: The full flag must assert if and only if count equals 4; it must not assert early.

cases.name: case08_pulse_width
cases.spec: When trigger is asserted, pulse must stay high for exactly two clock cycles including the trigger cycle.

golden_sva.expected_behavior: If trigger is sampled high, pulse must still be high one sampled cycle later, covering the required post-trigger hold cycle under the evaluator's sampled-state semantics.
golden_sva.temporal_type: non-overlapping implication with one-cycle delayed consequent (post-trigger hold check)

cases.name: case09_addr_increment
cases.spec: Address increments by 4 on every rising clock edge when step is high.

golden_sva.expected_behavior: If step was high in the previous sampled cycle, the current sampled address must equal the previous sampled address plus 4 and remain word-aligned.
golden_sva.temporal_type: overlapping implication with history reference (registered stride-and-alignment check)

cases.name: case10_hold_valid_until_ready
cases.spec: After fire, valid_o must remain asserted until a cycle where ready_i is high and handshake completes.

golden_sva.sva: assert property (@(posedge clk) disable iff (!rst_n) (valid_o && !ready_i) |=> (valid_o || ready_i));
golden_sva.expected_behavior: If valid_o is high while ready_i is low, then on the next sampled cycle either valid_o must still be high or ready_i must have risen to complete the handshake.
